hyps.why: If edge 0 is none, node 1 receives no signal so a conv on edge 4 sits on a dead path and adds nothing.
Edge 2 needs node 1 to carry signal, which edge 0 = none prevents.
Removing edge 4 costs nothing when node 1 is already dead, whereas it normally removes a useful path.
Removing edge 2 is harmless when node 1 receives no signal, but normally loses a useful path.
Replacing none with a conv restores a direct input-to-output path and gains more than upgrading an existing op.
Restoring a direct shortcut with a skip yields a bigger gain than swapping one existing op for another.
Reconnecting node 2 to the output with a 3x3 conv restores a whole branch, a bigger gain than upgrading an existing op.
A 1x1 conv after a severed parent is on a dead path and gives no benefit.
Adding a direct 0->3 conv where none existed gains more than refining an op already on that edge.
Turning a missing edge into a 3x3 conv adds both connectivity and capacity, beyond the average upgrade.
